clue.text: Begin to strike the lady over there

indicators.note: Begin points at the opening letter of the word that follows it, to

parts.note: to strike is to hit
her is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: Someone urges a woman far away to start a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin to strike' reads as starting a walkout, but 'Begin' takes only the first letter of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thither is an old adverb meaning to or towards that place, so far away from here.

clue.text: Staggers about with small animal in a back street

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the letters for street
back means the abbreviation for street is read in reverse

parts.note: an otter is a small river mammal

explanation.surface: A small creature wobbles about in an alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a back street' looks like an alley, but 'back' is an instruction: the street abbreviation is reversed and wrapped around the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, as if about to fall.

clue.text: Treats bad habits very badly

parts.note: read as a phrase meaning mistreats: harmful practices or wrong handling, described as bad ways of using something

explanation.surface: A therapist deals clumsily with a patient's vices.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-use someone is to treat them cruelly; the words read literally as bad employments.

clue.text: Lift up one in an enormous crowd

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a great multitude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is raised aloft within a huge throng.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise something, often with ropes or tackle.

clue.text: Keeping a bit back for making a booking

definitions.meaning: arranging a seat or table in advance

explanation.surface: Holding a little in reserve when booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something back is to keep it in store, and to book a seat ahead is to secure it in advance.

clue.text: One of a pair of airlines

definitions.text: One of a pair of airlines

parts.words: One of a pair of airlines
parts.note: read 'airlines' as two words, air lines: passages the breath travels through, of which every face has two

explanation.surface: A company that is one half of an airline partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is a channel for breathing in and out, and people have two of them.

clue.text: Detects a direction among those voting against

indicators.note: among puts the direction letter inside the word for the votes against

parts.note: the noes are those who vote no
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tendency among the opponents in a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose something out is to sniff it out, discover it.

clue.text: The clarity of a Kent town

definitions.meaning: transparency, as of a very thin fabric
a port on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: The bright air of a seaside town in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer cloth is so thin you can see through it, and the town of that name is a Thames-estuary port in Kent.

clue.text: Keeps a nastier mixture

indicators.note: mixture tells us the letters of the word nastier are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to an even more unpleasant blend.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to hold onto it.

clue.text: Found out how the student got paid

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
earned means received as payment

explanation.surface: Someone discovers how a student managed to make some money.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plate British student drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned means discovered or came to know.

clue.text: Agrees with Tom's first friends

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Tom's just before it

parts.note: allies are friends who stand together

explanation.surface: Tom's closest companions go along with him.
explanation.definitionFit: When accounts or stories tally they match up, which is to say they correspond.

clue.text: Get the aspect right for split ting up the light colours

indicators.note: splitting up (printed with a space) tells us the letters of the word before are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on placing a prism to break white light into its bands of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'split ting'; read it as 'splitting up', the anagram signal working on ASPECT plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are the bands of rainbow hues that white light separates into through a prism.

clue.text: Simple phraseology used to encourage an impoverished customer

definitions.text: used to encourage an impoverished customer
definitions.meaning: a payment plan in small instalments, offered to someone short of cash

explanation.surface: A salesman uses plain language to tempt a hard-up shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain wording is a matter of easy words, and an instalment plan offers buyers gentle repayment conditions.

clue.text: Preside with gravity within the constraint

indicators.note: within says the gravity letter is placed inside the word for constraint

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint
G is the physics symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A judge presides solemnly while staying within set limits.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule or hold sway, as a monarch presides over a realm.

clue.text: One lass tied up with fibre

indicators.note: tied up suggests letters knotted into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl is bound up with string.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and twine.

clue.text: I'll get him moved into the public gaze

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters of the words before are shifted around

explanation.surface: A promoter vows to push a performer into the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Limelight was the bright stage lamp of old theatres, hence public attention.

clue.text: At the wicket for 500-but got more

parts.note: a cricket batsman at the wicket stands in his crease, the line marked in front of the stumps
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A cricketer batting for a huge score added still more runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line where the batsman stands, so 'at the wicket' gives IN CREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Increased means grew larger or rose in amount.

clue.text: She is happy with only a low score

definitions.text: She is happy with only a low score

parts.words: She is happy with only a low score
parts.note: a score here is a musical part: a woman content to sing only the lowest line

explanation.surface: A woman cheerfully accepts a poor mark in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest female singing voice, so its singer takes the low part of the music.

clue.text: Tramping around with a game bird

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of the words beside it are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: A hiker walking about comes across a grouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, shot for sport.

clue.text: Support round about a thousand-that's first class

indicators.note: round says the support word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a pier is a pillar that holds up a bridge
re means about or concerning
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand pillars encircle something deemed top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means foremost or leading in rank.

clue.text: Grant forgiveness to the sailor and provide a solution

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common word for a sailor
to solve is to find the answer

explanation.surface: A priest pardons a seaman and sorts out his problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to pardon them, freeing them from guilt.

clue.text: Brush up on the area of bushes

definitions.meaning: to clean hard with a brush

explanation.surface: Someone revises their knowledge of shrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour with a stiff brush is to scrub, and scrubland is ground covered in low bushes.

clue.text: They learn about adders but don't take one note

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: don't take signals that a letter is left out of the word adders

parts.note: D is one of the notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Students study snakes but skip a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't take' removes only one of the two identical note letters from the snakes, not both.
explanation.definitionFit: Readers pick up knowledge from what they read.

clue.text: Sleep on what sounds like items for sale

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the letters come from how the clue phrase is said

parts.note: buys are things bought, bargains, doubled to give the sound wanted

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off over a catalogue of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Bye-byes is a nursery word for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-byes is a child's word for going to sleep.

clue.text: Take out lease to support the picture

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word lease are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Renting a place to show off a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand an artist props a canvas on.

clue.text: Very good speed, at the beginning

parts.note: first means at the start, as in 'first of all'
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A runner sets a fine pace from the start of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first-rate is of the highest class, excellent.

clue.text: The weakness of a useless structure

definitions.meaning: foolishness, a weak point of judgement
an ornamental building with no practical use, built for show on an estate

explanation.surface: A frailty is likened to a pointless building.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishness is folly, and so is an extravagant decorative building on an estate.

clue.text: Symbol to have met up with

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word met is read bottom to top, so reversed

explanation.surface: A badge to show you have met up with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem revered by a clan or group.

clue.text: I shall send a note to girl although this not permitted

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
E is one of the notes of the musical scale
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A man plans to send a forbidden message to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means against the law, forbidden.

clue.text: Let Tory group arrange a national one

indicators.note: arrange tells us the letters of the words before are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Conservative party faction organises an event.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the UK's National Lottery, the state-licensed prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's National Lottery is the state-run draw for cash prizes.

clue.text: Round about ten stumbling on the railway hoping to find the way in again

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: stumbling suggests letters lurching out of their order

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Around ten o'clock someone staggers along the tracks looking for the entrance back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' looks like a drunk on the tracks; it is the anagram signal for 'ten' alone, set between the 'about' and 'railway' abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is the act of coming back in, as a spacecraft returns into the atmosphere.

clue.text: Round moss is harmed by the diffusion of liquid

parts.note: O is a round shape

indicators.note: harmed means damaged, so the letters of the words before are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Moss growing in a ring is damaged when water seeps through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmed' looks like the plant being damaged, but it only tells us to shuffle the two words before it, which go after the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the passage of a solvent through a membrane, a kind of seepage between solutions.
